And al-Tirmidhi said: 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, Shababah narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Ala', from al-Dahhak ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Arzam al-Ash'ari, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah saying: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The first thing a servant will be questioned about of the bounty on the Day of Resurrection is that it will be said to him: Did We not make your body healthy, and give you cool water to drink?"

Related by al-Tirmidhi alone. Ibn Hibban related it in his Sahih by way of al-Walid ibn Muslim, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Ala' ibn Zabr, with the same wording.

And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Musaddad narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Yahya ibn Hatib, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: al-Zubayr said: When the verse "[Then] you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty" was revealed, they said: O Messenger of Allah, about which bounty will we be questioned, when there are only the two black things, dates and water? He said: "Indeed, that will come to pass." Likewise al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah related it from the hadith of Sufyan, that is Ibn 'Uyaynah, with the same wording. Ahmad related it from him. And al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan.

And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Zahrani narrated to us, Hafs ibn 'Umar al-'Adani narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from 'Ikrimah, who said: When this verse was revealed: "Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty," the Companions said: O Messenger of Allah, what bounty are we in, when we eat only barley bread in the halves of our stomachs? Then Allah revealed to His Prophet (ﷺ): Say to them: Do you not wear sandals and drink cold water? That is of the bounty.

And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn al-Asbahani informed us, from Ibn Abi Layla, I think from 'Amir, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning His saying: "[Then] you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty," he said: "Security and health." [Abd Allah ibn Ahmad related it in Zawa'id al-Zuhd (855) by way of Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Asbahani, with the same chain.]

And Zayd ibn Aslam said, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty," meaning: the fullness of stomachs, cold drink, shade of dwellings, soundness of bodies, and the pleasure of sleep. Ibn Abi Hatim related it with his earlier chain, from him, at the beginning of the surah.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Even concerning a sip of honey. Mujahid said: Concerning every pleasure of the pleasures of this world. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: The bounty of lunch and dinner. Abu Qilabah said: Among the bounties is eating honey and ghee with pure bread. The saying of Mujahid is the most comprehensive of these sayings.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning "Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty": He said: The bounty is the health of bodies, hearing and sight; Allah will question the servants about how they used them, and He knows that better than they do. This is His saying, may He be exalted: "Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart – all of those will be questioned about" (al-Isra' 17:36).

It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari, Sunan al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, by way of 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Hind, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam) said: "Two blessings many people are cheated in: health and free time."

The meaning of this is that they fall short in thanking these two blessings; they do not fulfil their due, and whoever does not fulfil the right that is incumbent upon him is cheated.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Marwazi narrated to us, 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, Abu Hamzah narrated to us, from Layth, from Abu Fazarah, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What is above the waist-wrap, the shade of a wall, and bread, for which the servant will be reckoned on the Day of Resurrection, or will be questioned about." [Musnad al-Bazzar (3643), Kashf al-Astar; Layth ibn Abi Sulaym is weak.] Then he said: We do not know it except through this chain.

And Imam Ahmad said: Bahz and 'Affan narrated to us, both said: Hammad narrated to us – 'Affan said in his narration: – Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says – 'Affan said: on the Day of Resurrection –: O son of Adam, I carried you upon horses and camels, I married you to women, and I made you enjoy and lead; so where is the thanks for that?" [Musnad Ahmad (2/492).] He alone related it by this route.

End of the tafsir of Surah "al-Takathur" [ and to Allah belongs all praise and grace ].

**Tafsir (commentary on) Surat at-Takathur**
It is a Meccan surah.
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
* *

He, may He be exalted, says: The love of this world, its pleasures and its splendour, has preoccupied you away from seeking the Hereafter and striving for it. That continued until death came to you, you visited the graves, and you became among their inhabitants?!

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Waqqar al-Misri narrated to us, Khalid ibn Abd ad-Dayim narrated to us, from Ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you﴾ from obedience, ﴿until you visit the graves﴾ until death comes to you."[[This is mu'dal (a narration with two or more consecutive narrators missing), and Abd ar-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam is weak.]]

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you﴾ refers to wealth and children.

In Sahih al-Bukhari, in its chapter "ar-Riqaq" (softening of hearts), there is: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b who said: "We used to regard this as part of the Qur'an until the revelation of ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you﴾," meaning: "If the son of Adam had a valley of gold..."

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'ba narrated to us: I heard Qatadah narrating from Mutarrif, meaning Ibn Abd Allah ibn ash-Shikhkhir, from his father, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was reciting: "﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you﴾. The son of Adam says: 'My wealth, my wealth.' But do you have from your wealth except what you eat and thereby consume, or what you wear and thereby wear out, or what you give in charity and thereby send ahead?"

Muslim, at-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i narrated it through the route of Shu'ba, with the same wording.[[Al-Musnad (4/24), Sahih Muslim no. (2958), Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (3354), and Sunan an-Nasa'i (6/238).]]

Muslim said in his Sahih: Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Hafs ibn Maysara narrated to us, from al-Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The servant says: 'My wealth, my wealth?' Of his wealth he has only three things: what he eats and thereby consumes, what he wears and thereby wears out, and what he gives in charity and thereby stores up. Everything else will go away, and he will leave it for the people." Muslim alone narrated it.[[Sahih Muslim no. (2959).]]

Al-Bukhari said: Al-Humaydi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm narrated to us, that he heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three things follow the deceased: two return and one remains with him. His family and his wealth follow him, and then his family and his wealth return, while his deeds remain."

Muslim, at-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i also narrated it through the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyayna, with the same wording.[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6514), Sahih Muslim no. (2960), Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (2379), and as-Sunan al-Kubra of an-Nasa'i no. (2064).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya narrated to us, from Shu'ba, Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The son of Adam grows old, and two things remain in him: greed and hope." Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it in their Sahihs.[[Al-Musnad (3/115), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6421), and Sahih Muslim no. (1047).]]

Al-Hafiz (the memorizer of hadith) Ibn Asakir mentioned, in the biography of al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, whose name was ad-Dahhak, that he saw a man holding a dirham, and said: "Whose is this dirham?" The man said: "Mine." He said: "It is yours only if you spend it on a reward or seeking gratitude." Then al-Ahnaf recited, quoting a line of a poet:

"You belong to wealth if you hold onto it,
but when you spend it, the wealth belongs to you."[[Tarikh Dimashq (8/443, manuscript).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Usama narrated to us, saying: Salih ibn Hayyan narrated to me, from Ibn Buraydah, concerning His words ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you﴾: it was revealed about two tribes of the Ansar, the Banu Harithah and the Banu al-Harith, who boasted to one another and competed in numbers. One of them said: "Among you is such-and-such the son of such-and-such, and such-and-such?" The others said the same. They boasted about their living members. Then they said: "Come, let us go to the graves." Each group began saying: "Among you is such-and-such?" pointing to a grave, "and such-and-such?" The others did likewise. So Allah revealed: ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you, until you visit the graves﴾, meaning: in what you have seen there is a lesson and a preoccupation.

Qatadah said: ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you, until you visit the graves﴾: They used to say, "We are more numerous than the Banu so-and-so, and we are more numerous than the Banu so-and-so," while they were falling away day by day until the end of them. By Allah, they continued like this until they all became people of the graves.

The correct view is that the meaning of His words ﴿you visit the graves﴾ is: you go to them and are buried in them. This is as is found in the Sahih: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon a Bedouin man to visit him when he was ill. He said: "Do not worry, it is a purification, if Allah wills." The man said: "A purification? Rather, it is a boiling fever upon an old man, which will bring him to the graves!" He said: "Then so be it."[[Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (5662, 5656, 7470).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'a narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Asbahani narrated to us, Hakkam ibn Salm ar-Razi informed us, from Amr ibn Abi Qays, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Minhal, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ali, who said: "We continued to doubt the punishment of the grave until the revelation of ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you, until you visit the graves﴾."

At-Tirmidhi narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Hakkam ibn Salm, with the same wording, and said: It is gharib (a hadith with a single narration path).[[Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (3355).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Salama ibn Dawud al-Ursi narrated to us, Abu al-Malih ar-Raqqi narrated to us, from Maymun ibn Mihran, who said: I was sitting with Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz when he recited ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you, until you visit the graves﴾. He paused for a while, then said: "O Maymun, I do not see the graves except as a visit, and the visitor must return to his home."

Abu Muhammad (Ibn Abi Hatim) said: That is, he must return to his home, which is either Paradise or Hellfire. It is also related that a Bedouin heard a man reciting this verse, ﴿until you visit the graves﴾, and said: "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, the people have been resurrected today!" meaning that the visitor will move from that place to another.
* *

As for His words: ﴿No! You will soon know. Then, no! You will soon know﴾, al-Hasan al-Basri said: This is a warning upon a warning.

Ad-Dahhak said: ﴿No! You will soon know﴾ means: the disbelievers; ﴿Then, no! You will soon know﴾ means: O believers.
* *

As for His words: ﴿No! If you knew with certainty of knowledge﴾, meaning: if you knew with the true knowledge, the rivalry in worldly increase would not have diverted you from seeking the Abode of the Hereafter until you went to the graves.

Then He said: ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire. Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾. This is an explanation of the earlier warning, His words ﴿No! You will soon know. Then, no! You will soon know﴾. He threatened them with this state, which is seeing the Fire. When it breathes out a single breath, every angel brought near and every messenger sent will fall to their knees out of awe, grandeur, and witnessing the terrors, as is related in the transmitted report concerning this.
* *

As for His words: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, meaning: then you will surely be questioned that Day about giving thanks for what Allah has bestowed upon you, such as health, security, provision, and other things, and whether you met His blessings with thanks and worship.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'a narrated to us, Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz al-Muqri narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Isa Abu Khalid al-Khazzaz narrated to us, Yunus ibn Ubayd narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that he heard Umar ibn al-Khattab say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out at midday and found Abu Bakr in the mosque. He said: "What brought you out at this hour?" He said: "What brought you out, O Messenger of Allah, brought me out." Then Umar ibn al-Khattab came, and he said: "What brought you out, O son of al-Khattab?" He said: "What brought you out brought me out." Umar sat down, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began speaking with them both. Then he said: "Do you have the strength to go to this palm grove and obtain food, drink and shade?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Go with us to the house of Ibn at-Tayyihan, Abu al-Haytham al-Ansari." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went ahead of us, greeted and asked permission three times, while Umm al-Haytham was behind the door listening to the speech, wishing that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would increase her greeting. When he wanted to leave, Umm al-Haytham came out running after them and said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I heard your greeting, but I wanted you to increase your greeting to us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "May good be with you." Then he said: "Where is Abu al-Haytham? I do not see him." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, he is nearby; he went to fetch sweet water. Come in, for he will come shortly, if Allah wills." She spread a rug under a tree. Abu al-Haytham came, rejoiced at them, and his eyes were delighted by them. He climbed a palm tree and cut bunches for them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "That is enough, O Abu al-Haytham." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, eat from its unripe dates, its ripe dates, and its dried dates." Then he brought them water, and they drank. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is part of the bliss about which you will be questioned."[[Narrated by at-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (19/253) through the route of Zakariyya ibn Yahya, from Abd Allah ibn Isa, with the same wording. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/317): "In it is Abd Allah ibn Isa, Abu Khalaf, who is weak."]] This is gharib from this route.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Husayn ibn Ali as-Sada'i narrated to me, al-Walid ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Kaysan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: While Abu Bakr and Umar were sitting, the Prophet (ﷺ) came to them and said: "What has made you sit here?" They said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, we did not leave our homes except from hunger." He said: "By the One who sent me with the truth, nothing else brought me out." So they set out until they came to the house of a man from the Ansar. The woman met them, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to her: "Where is so-and-so?" She said: "He has gone to fetch sweet water for us." Then their host came carrying his water-skin and said: "Welcome! Nothing has visited the servants that is better than what has visited me today." He hung his water-skin on the trunk of a palm tree, went off, and brought them a bunch of dates. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Why did you not pick it yourself?" He said: "I wanted you to be those whom you choose with your own eyes." Then he took the knife. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the milk-giver." So he slaughtered for them that day, and they ate. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You will surely be questioned about this on the Day of Resurrection. Hunger brought you out of your homes, and you did not return until you obtained this. This is part of the bliss."[[Tafsir at-Tabari (30/185).]]

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Yazid ibn Kaysan, with the same wording.[[Sahih Muslim no. (2038).]] Abu Ya'la and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of al-Muharibi, from Yahya ibn Ubayd Allah, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, with the same wording.[[Musnad Abi Ya'la (1/79) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3181).]] The people of the four Sunan (collections) have also narrated it, through the hadith of Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayrah, with something similar to this context and this story.[[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (5128), Sunan at-Tirmidhi nos. (2822, 2369), as-Sunan al-Kubra of an-Nasa'i no. (11697), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3745).]]

And Imam Ahmad said: Surayj narrated to us, Hashraj narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu 'Usayb, who was the freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out at night and passed by me, and he called me, so I went out to him. Then he passed by Abu Bakr and called him, and he went out to him. Then he passed by 'Umar and called him, and he went out to him. So he set off until he came to a garden (ḥā'iṭ) belonging to one of the Ansar. He said to the owner of the garden: "Feed us." So he brought a cluster of dates (dhiq) and placed it down, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions ate. Then he asked for cold water and drank, and he said: "You will certainly be questioned about this on the Day of Resurrection." He said: So 'Umar took the cluster and struck it against the ground, until the unripe dates (busr) scattered before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then he said: O Messenger of Allah, will we really be questioned about this on the Day of Resurrection? He said: "Yes, except for three things: a piece of cloth with which a man covers his private parts, or a morsel with which he stills his hunger, or a hole into which he enters to shelter from heat and cold." Related by Ahmad alone.

And Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, 'Ammar narrated to us, I heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu Bakr and 'Umar ate fresh dates (ruṭab) and drank water, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is of the bounty (naʿīm) about which you will be questioned."

Al-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah [from 'Ammar ibn Abi 'Ammar, from Jabir] with the same wording.

And Imam Ahmad said: Ahmad narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Mahmud ibn al-Rabi' who said: When the verse "Competition in worldly gain diverts you" was revealed, and he recited until he reached "Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty," they said: O Messenger of Allah, about which bounty will we be questioned? Indeed, there are only the two black things: water and dates, and our swords are on our necks, and the enemy is present. About which bounty will we be questioned? He said: "Indeed, that will come to pass."

And Ahmad said: Abu 'Amir 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Habib narrated to us, from his father, from his paternal uncle, who said: We were in a gathering when the Prophet (ﷺ) came upon us, and there was a trace of water on his head. We said: O Messenger of Allah, we see you in good spirits. He said: "Indeed." He said: Then the people began to discuss wealth (ghinā), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no harm in wealth for one who fears Allah, and health for one who fears Allah is better than wealth, and contentment of the soul (ṭīb al-nafs) is of the bounty."

Ibn Majah related it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Khalid ibn Makhlad, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman, with the same chain. [Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/158): "This chain is ṣaḥīḥ, its narrators are trustworthy."]

Related by al-Tirmidhi alone. Ibn Hibban related it in his Sahih by way of al-Walid ibn Muslim, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Ala' ibn Zabr, with the same wording.

And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Musaddad narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Yahya ibn Hatib, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: al-Zubayr said: When the verse "[Then] you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty" was revealed, they said: O Messenger of Allah, about which bounty will we be questioned, when there are only the two black things, dates and water? And al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan.

And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Zahrani narrated to us, Hafs ibn 'Umar al-'Adani narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from 'Ikrimah, who said: When this verse was revealed: "Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty," the Companions said: O Messenger of Allah, what bounty are we in, when we eat only barley bread in the halves of our stomachs? And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn al-Asbahani informed us, from Ibn Abi Layla, I think from 'Amir, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning His saying: "[Then] you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty," he said: "Security and health." [Abd Allah ibn Ahmad related it in Zawa'id al-Zuhd (855) by way of Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Asbahani, with the same chain.]

And Zayd ibn Aslam said, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty," meaning: the fullness of stomachs, cold drink, shade of dwellings, soundness of bodies, and the pleasure of sleep. It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari, Sunan al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, by way of 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Hind, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam) said: "Two blessings many people are cheated in: health and free time."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

He, may He be exalted, says: The love of this world, its pleasures and its splendour, has preoccupied you away from seeking the Hereafter and striving for it. That continued until death came to you, you visited the graves, and you became among their inhabitants?!

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Waqqar al-Misri narrated to us, Khalid ibn Abd ad-Dayim narrated to us, from Ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you﴾ from obedience, ﴿until you visit the graves﴾ until death comes to you."[[This is mu'dal (a narration with two or more consecutive narrators missing), and Abd ar-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam is weak.]]

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you﴾ refers to wealth and children.

In Sahih al-Bukhari, in its chapter "ar-Riqaq" (softening of hearts), there is: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b who said: "We used to regard this as part of the Qur'an until the revelation of ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you﴾," meaning: "If the son of Adam had a valley of gold..."

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'ba narrated to us: I heard Qatadah narrating from Mutarrif, meaning Ibn Abd Allah ibn ash-Shikhkhir, from his father, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was reciting: "﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you﴾. The son of Adam says: 'My wealth, my wealth.' But do you have from your wealth except what you eat and thereby consume, or what you wear and thereby wear out, or what you give in charity and thereby send ahead?"

Muslim, at-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i narrated it through the route of Shu'ba, with the same wording.[[Al-Musnad (4/24), Sahih Muslim no. (2958), Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (3354), and Sunan an-Nasa'i (6/238).]]

Muslim said in his Sahih: Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Hafs ibn Maysara narrated to us, from al-Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The servant says: 'My wealth, my wealth?' Of his wealth he has only three things: what he eats and thereby consumes, what he wears and thereby wears out, and what he gives in charity and thereby stores up. Everything else will go away, and he will leave it for the people." Muslim alone narrated it.[[Sahih Muslim no. (2959).]]

Al-Bukhari said: Al-Humaydi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm narrated to us, that he heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three things follow the deceased: two return and one remains with him. His family and his wealth follow him, and then his family and his wealth return, while his deeds remain."

Muslim, at-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i also narrated it through the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyayna, with the same wording.[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6514), Sahih Muslim no. (2960), Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (2379), and as-Sunan al-Kubra of an-Nasa'i no. (2064).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya narrated to us, from Shu'ba, Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The son of Adam grows old, and two things remain in him: greed and hope." Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it in their Sahihs.[[Al-Musnad (3/115), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6421), and Sahih Muslim no. (1047).]]

Al-Hafiz (the memorizer of hadith) Ibn Asakir mentioned, in the biography of al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, whose name was ad-Dahhak, that he saw a man holding a dirham, and said: "Whose is this dirham?" The man said: "Mine." He said: "It is yours only if you spend it on a reward or seeking gratitude." Then al-Ahnaf recited, quoting a line of a poet:

"You belong to wealth if you hold onto it,
but when you spend it, the wealth belongs to you."[[Tarikh Dimashq (8/443, manuscript).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Usama narrated to us, saying: Salih ibn Hayyan narrated to me, from Ibn Buraydah, concerning His words ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you﴾: it was revealed about two tribes of the Ansar, the Banu Harithah and the Banu al-Harith, who boasted to one another and competed in numbers. One of them said: "Among you is such-and-such the son of such-and-such, and such-and-such?" The others said the same. They boasted about their living members. Then they said: "Come, let us go to the graves." Each group began saying: "Among you is such-and-such?" pointing to a grave, "and such-and-such?" The others did likewise. So Allah revealed: ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you, until you visit the graves﴾, meaning: in what you have seen there is a lesson and a preoccupation.

Qatadah said: ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you, until you visit the graves﴾: They used to say, "We are more numerous than the Banu so-and-so, and we are more numerous than the Banu so-and-so," while they were falling away day by day until the end of them. By Allah, they continued like this until they all became people of the graves.

The correct view is that the meaning of His words ﴿you visit the graves﴾ is: you go to them and are buried in them. This is as is found in the Sahih: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon a Bedouin man to visit him when he was ill. He said: "Do not worry, it is a purification, if Allah wills." The man said: "A purification? Rather, it is a boiling fever upon an old man, which will bring him to the graves!" He said: "Then so be it."[[Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (5662, 5656, 7470).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'a narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Asbahani narrated to us, Hakkam ibn Salm ar-Razi informed us, from Amr ibn Abi Qays, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Minhal, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ali, who said: "We continued to doubt the punishment of the grave until the revelation of ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you, until you visit the graves﴾."

At-Tirmidhi narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Hakkam ibn Salm, with the same wording, and said: It is gharib (a hadith with a single narration path).[[Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (3355).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Salama ibn Dawud al-Ursi narrated to us, Abu al-Malih ar-Raqqi narrated to us, from Maymun ibn Mihran, who said: I was sitting with Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz when he recited ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you, until you visit the graves﴾. He paused for a while, then said: "O Maymun, I do not see the graves except as a visit, and the visitor must return to his home."

Abu Muhammad (Ibn Abi Hatim) said: That is, he must return to his home, which is either Paradise or Hellfire. It is also related that a Bedouin heard a man reciting this verse, ﴿until you visit the graves﴾, and said: "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, the people have been resurrected today!" meaning that the visitor will move from that place to another.
* *

As for His words: ﴿No! You will soon know. Then, no! You will soon know﴾, al-Hasan al-Basri said: This is a warning upon a warning.

Ad-Dahhak said: ﴿No! You will soon know﴾ means: the disbelievers; ﴿Then, no! You will soon know﴾ means: O believers.
* *

As for His words: ﴿No! If you knew with certainty of knowledge﴾, meaning: if you knew with the true knowledge, the rivalry in worldly increase would not have diverted you from seeking the Abode of the Hereafter until you went to the graves.

Then He said: ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire. Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾. This is an explanation of the earlier warning, His words ﴿No! You will soon know. Then, no! You will soon know﴾. He threatened them with this state, which is seeing the Fire. When it breathes out a single breath, every angel brought near and every messenger sent will fall to their knees out of awe, grandeur, and witnessing the terrors, as is related in the transmitted report concerning this.
* *

As for His words: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, meaning: then you will surely be questioned that Day about giving thanks for what Allah has bestowed upon you, such as health, security, provision, and other things, and whether you met His blessings with thanks and worship.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'a narrated to us, Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz al-Muqri narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Isa Abu Khalid al-Khazzaz narrated to us, Yunus ibn Ubayd narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that he heard Umar ibn al-Khattab say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out at midday and found Abu Bakr in the mosque. He said: "What brought you out at this hour?" He said: "What brought you out, O Messenger of Allah, brought me out." Then Umar ibn al-Khattab came, and he said: "What brought you out, O son of al-Khattab?" He said: "What brought you out brought me out." Umar sat down, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began speaking with them both. Then he said: "Do you have the strength to go to this palm grove and obtain food, drink and shade?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Go with us to the house of Ibn at-Tayyihan, Abu al-Haytham al-Ansari." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went ahead of us, greeted and asked permission three times, while Umm al-Haytham was behind the door listening to the speech, wishing that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would increase her greeting. When he wanted to leave, Umm al-Haytham came out running after them and said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I heard your greeting, but I wanted you to increase your greeting to us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "May good be with you." Then he said: "Where is Abu al-Haytham? I do not see him." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, he is nearby; he went to fetch sweet water. Come in, for he will come shortly, if Allah wills." She spread a rug under a tree. Abu al-Haytham came, rejoiced at them, and his eyes were delighted by them. He climbed a palm tree and cut bunches for them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "That is enough, O Abu al-Haytham." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, eat from its unripe dates, its ripe dates, and its dried dates." Then he brought them water, and they drank. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is part of the bliss about which you will be questioned."[[Narrated by at-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (19/253) through the route of Zakariyya ibn Yahya, from Abd Allah ibn Isa, with the same wording. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/317): "In it is Abd Allah ibn Isa, Abu Khalaf, who is weak."]] This is gharib from this route.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Husayn ibn Ali as-Sada'i narrated to me, al-Walid ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Kaysan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: While Abu Bakr and Umar were sitting, the Prophet (ﷺ) came to them and said: "What has made you sit here?" They said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, we did not leave our homes except from hunger." He said: "By the One who sent me with the truth, nothing else brought me out." So they set out until they came to the house of a man from the Ansar. The woman met them, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to her: "Where is so-and-so?" She said: "He has gone to fetch sweet water for us." Then their host came carrying his water-skin and said: "Welcome! Nothing has visited the servants that is better than what has visited me today." He hung his water-skin on the trunk of a palm tree, went off, and brought them a bunch of dates. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Why did you not pick it yourself?" He said: "I wanted you to be those whom you choose with your own eyes." Then he took the knife. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the milk-giver." So he slaughtered for them that day, and they ate. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You will surely be questioned about this on the Day of Resurrection. Hunger brought you out of your homes, and you did not return until you obtained this. This is part of the bliss."[[Tafsir at-Tabari (30/185).]]

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Yazid ibn Kaysan, with the same wording.[[Sahih Muslim no. (2038).]] Abu Ya'la and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of al-Muharibi, from Yahya ibn Ubayd Allah, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, with the same wording.[[Musnad Abi Ya'la (1/79) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3181).]] The people of the four Sunan (collections) have also narrated it, through the hadith of Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayrah, with something similar to this context and this story.[[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (5128), Sunan at-Tirmidhi nos. (2822, 2369), as-Sunan al-Kubra of an-Nasa'i no. (11697), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3745).]]

And Imam Ahmad said: Surayj narrated to us, Hashraj narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu 'Usayb, who was the freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out at night and passed by me, and he called me, so I went out to him. Then he passed by Abu Bakr and called him, and he went out to him. Then he passed by 'Umar and called him, and he went out to him. So he set off until he came to a garden (ḥā'iṭ) belonging to one of the Ansar. He said to the owner of the garden: "Feed us." So he brought a cluster of dates (dhiq) and placed it down, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions ate. Then he asked for cold water and drank, and he said: "You will certainly be questioned about this on the Day of Resurrection." He said: So 'Umar took the cluster and struck it against the ground, until the unripe dates (busr) scattered before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then he said: O Messenger of Allah, will we really be questioned about this on the Day of Resurrection? He said: "Yes, except for three things: a piece of cloth with which a man covers his private parts, or a morsel with which he stills his hunger, or a hole into which he enters to shelter from heat and cold." Related by Ahmad alone.

And Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, 'Ammar narrated to us, I heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu Bakr and 'Umar ate fresh dates (ruṭab) and drank water, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is of the bounty (naʿīm) about which you will be questioned."

Al-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah [from 'Ammar ibn Abi 'Ammar, from Jabir] with the same wording.

And Imam Ahmad said: Ahmad narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Mahmud ibn al-Rabi' who said: When the verse "Competition in worldly gain diverts you" was revealed, and he recited until he reached "Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty," they said: O Messenger of Allah, about which bounty will we be questioned? Indeed, there are only the two black things: water and dates, and our swords are on our necks, and the enemy is present. About which bounty will we be questioned? He said: "Indeed, that will come to pass."

And Ahmad said: Abu 'Amir 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Habib narrated to us, from his father, from his paternal uncle, who said: We were in a gathering when the Prophet (ﷺ) came upon us, and there was a trace of water on his head. We said: O Messenger of Allah, we see you in good spirits. He said: "Indeed." He said: Then the people began to discuss wealth (ghinā), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no harm in wealth for one who fears Allah, and health for one who fears Allah is better than wealth, and contentment of the soul (ṭīb al-nafs) is of the bounty."

Ibn Majah related it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Khalid ibn Makhlad, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman, with the same chain. [Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/158): "This chain is ṣaḥīḥ, its narrators are trustworthy."]

And al-Tirmidhi said: 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, Shababah narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Ala', from al-Dahhak ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Arzam al-Ash'ari, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah saying: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The first thing a servant will be questioned about of the bounty on the Day of Resurrection is that it will be said to him: Did We not make your body healthy, and give you cool water to drink?"

Related by al-Tirmidhi alone. Ibn Hibban related it in his Sahih by way of al-Walid ibn Muslim, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Ala' ibn Zabr, with the same wording.

And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Musaddad narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Yahya ibn Hatib, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: al-Zubayr said: When the verse "[Then] you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty" was revealed, they said: O Messenger of Allah, about which bounty will we be questioned, when there are only the two black things, dates and water? He said: "Indeed, that will come to pass." Likewise al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah related it from the hadith of Sufyan, that is Ibn 'Uyaynah, with the same wording. Ahmad related it from him. And al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan.

And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Zahrani narrated to us, Hafs ibn 'Umar al-'Adani narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from 'Ikrimah, who said: When this verse was revealed: "Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty," the Companions said: O Messenger of Allah, what bounty are we in, when we eat only barley bread in the halves of our stomachs? Then Allah revealed to His Prophet (ﷺ): Say to them: Do you not wear sandals and drink cold water? That is of the bounty.

And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn al-Asbahani informed us, from Ibn Abi Layla, I think from 'Amir, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning His saying: "[Then] you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty," he said: "Security and health." [Abd Allah ibn Ahmad related it in Zawa'id al-Zuhd (855) by way of Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Asbahani, with the same chain.]

And Zayd ibn Aslam said, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty," meaning: the fullness of stomachs, cold drink, shade of dwellings, soundness of bodies, and the pleasure of sleep. Ibn Abi Hatim related it with his earlier chain, from him, at the beginning of the surah.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Even concerning a sip of honey. Mujahid said: Concerning every pleasure of the pleasures of this world. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: The bounty of lunch and dinner. Abu Qilabah said: Among the bounties is eating honey and ghee with pure bread. The saying of Mujahid is the most comprehensive of these sayings.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning "Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty": He said: The bounty is the health of bodies, hearing and sight; Allah will question the servants about how they used them, and He knows that better than they do. This is His saying, may He be exalted: "Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart – all of those will be questioned about" (al-Isra' 17:36).

It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari, Sunan al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, by way of 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Hind, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam) said: "Two blessings many people are cheated in: health and free time."

The meaning of this is that they fall short in thanking these two blessings; they do not fulfil their due, and whoever does not fulfil the right that is incumbent upon him is cheated.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Marwazi narrated to us, 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, Abu Hamzah narrated to us, from Layth, from Abu Fazarah, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What is above the waist-wrap, the shade of a wall, and bread, for which the servant will be reckoned on the Day of Resurrection, or will be questioned about." [Musnad al-Bazzar (3643), Kashf al-Astar; Layth ibn Abi Sulaym is weak.] Then he said: We do not know it except through this chain.

And Imam Ahmad said: Bahz and 'Affan narrated to us, both said: Hammad narrated to us – 'Affan said in his narration: – Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says – 'Affan said: on the Day of Resurrection –: O son of Adam, I carried you upon horses and camels, I married you to women, and I made you enjoy and lead; so where is the thanks for that?" [Musnad Ahmad (2/492).] He alone related it by this route.

End of the tafsir of Surah "al-Takathur" [ and to Allah belongs all praise and grace ].

The man said: "A purification? Rather, it is a boiling fever upon an old man, which will bring him to the graves!" He said: "Then so be it."[[Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (5662, 5656, 7470).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'a narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Asbahani narrated to us, Hakkam ibn Salm ar-Razi informed us, from Amr ibn Abi Qays, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Minhal, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ali, who said: "We continued to doubt the punishment of the grave until the revelation of ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you, until you visit the graves﴾."

At-Tirmidhi narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Hakkam ibn Salm, with the same wording, and said: It is gharib (a hadith with a single narration path).[[Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (3355).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Salama ibn Dawud al-Ursi narrated to us, Abu al-Malih ar-Raqqi narrated to us, from Maymun ibn Mihran, who said: I was sitting with Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz when he recited ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you, until you visit the graves﴾. He paused for a while, then said: "O Maymun, I do not see the graves except as a visit, and the visitor must return to his home."

Abu Muhammad (Ibn Abi Hatim) said: That is, he must return to his home, which is either Paradise or Hellfire. It is also related that a Bedouin heard a man reciting this verse, ﴿until you visit the graves﴾, and said: "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, the people have been resurrected today!" meaning that the visitor will move from that place to another.
* *

As for His words: ﴿No! You will soon know. Then, no! You will soon know﴾, al-Hasan al-Basri said: This is a warning upon a warning.

Ad-Dahhak said: ﴿No! You will soon know﴾ means: the disbelievers; ﴿Then, no! You will soon know﴾ means: O believers.
* *

As for His words: ﴿No! If you knew with certainty of knowledge﴾, meaning: if you knew with the true knowledge, the rivalry in worldly increase would not have diverted you from seeking the Abode of the Hereafter until you went to the graves.

Then He said: ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire. Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾. This is an explanation of the earlier warning, His words ﴿No! You will soon know. Then, no! You will soon know﴾. He threatened them with this state, which is seeing the Fire. When it breathes out a single breath, every angel brought near and every messenger sent will fall to their knees out of awe, grandeur, and witnessing the terrors, as is related in the transmitted report concerning this.
* *

As for His words: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, meaning: then you will surely be questioned that Day about giving thanks for what Allah has bestowed upon you, such as health, security, provision, and other things, and whether you met His blessings with thanks and worship.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'a narrated to us, Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz al-Muqri narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Isa Abu Khalid al-Khazzaz narrated to us, Yunus ibn Ubayd narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that he heard Umar ibn al-Khattab say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out at midday and found Abu Bakr in the mosque. He said: "What brought you out at this hour?" He said: "What brought you out, O Messenger of Allah, brought me out." Then Umar ibn al-Khattab came, and he said: "What brought you out, O son of al-Khattab?" He said: "What brought you out brought me out." Umar sat down, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began speaking with them both. Then he said: "Do you have the strength to go to this palm grove and obtain food, drink and shade?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Go with us to the house of Ibn at-Tayyihan, Abu al-Haytham al-Ansari." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went ahead of us, greeted and asked permission three times, while Umm al-Haytham was behind the door listening to the speech, wishing that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would increase her greeting. When he wanted to leave, Umm al-Haytham came out running after them and said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I heard your greeting, but I wanted you to increase your greeting to us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "May good be with you." Then he said: "Where is Abu al-Haytham? I do not see him." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, he is nearby; he went to fetch sweet water. Come in, for he will come shortly, if Allah wills." She spread a rug under a tree. Abu al-Haytham came, rejoiced at them, and his eyes were delighted by them. He climbed a palm tree and cut bunches for them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "That is enough, O Abu al-Haytham." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, eat from its unripe dates, its ripe dates, and its dried dates." Then he brought them water, and they drank. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is part of the bliss about which you will be questioned."[[Narrated by at-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (19/253) through the route of Zakariyya ibn Yahya, from Abd Allah ibn Isa, with the same wording. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/317): "In it is Abd Allah ibn Isa, Abu Khalaf, who is weak."]] This is gharib from this route.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Husayn ibn Ali as-Sada'i narrated to me, al-Walid ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Kaysan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: While Abu Bakr and Umar were sitting, the Prophet (ﷺ) came to them and said: "What has made you sit here?" They said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, we did not leave our homes except from hunger." He said: "By the One who sent me with the truth, nothing else brought me out." So they set out until they came to the house of a man from the Ansar. The woman met them, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to her: "Where is so-and-so?" She said: "He has gone to fetch sweet water for us." Then their host came carrying his water-skin and said: "Welcome! Nothing has visited the servants that is better than what has visited me today." He hung his water-skin on the trunk of a palm tree, went off, and brought them a bunch of dates. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Why did you not pick it yourself?" He said: "I wanted you to be those whom you choose with your own eyes." Then he took the knife. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the milk-giver." So he slaughtered for them that day, and they ate. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You will surely be questioned about this on the Day of Resurrection. Hunger brought you out of your homes, and you did not return until you obtained this. This is part of the bliss."[[Tafsir at-Tabari (30/185).]]

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Yazid ibn Kaysan, with the same wording.[[Sahih Muslim no. (2038).]] Abu Ya'la and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of al-Muharibi, from Yahya ibn Ubayd Allah, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, with the same wording.[[Musnad Abi Ya'la (1/79) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3181).]] The people of the four Sunan (collections) have also narrated it, through the hadith of Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayrah, with something similar to this context and this story.[[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (5128), Sunan at-Tirmidhi nos. (2822, 2369), as-Sunan al-Kubra of an-Nasa'i no. (11697), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3745).]]

And Imam Ahmad said: Surayj narrated to us, Hashraj narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu 'Usayb, who was the freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out at night and passed by me, and he called me, so I went out to him. Then he passed by Abu Bakr and called him, and he went out to him. Then he passed by 'Umar and called him, and he went out to him. So he set off until he came to a garden (ḥā'iṭ) belonging to one of the Ansar. He said to the owner of the garden: "Feed us." So he brought a cluster of dates (dhiq) and placed it down, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions ate. Then he asked for cold water and drank, and he said: "You will certainly be questioned about this on the Day of Resurrection." He said: So 'Umar took the cluster and struck it against the ground, until the unripe dates (busr) scattered before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then he said: O Messenger of Allah, will we really be questioned about this on the Day of Resurrection? He said: "Yes, except for three things: a piece of cloth with which a man covers his private parts, or a morsel with which he stills his hunger, or a hole into which he enters to shelter from heat and cold." Related by Ahmad alone.

And Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, 'Ammar narrated to us, I heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu Bakr and 'Umar ate fresh dates (ruṭab) and drank water, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is of the bounty (naʿīm) about which you will be questioned."

Al-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah [from 'Ammar ibn Abi 'Ammar, from Jabir] with the same wording.

And Imam Ahmad said: Ahmad narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Mahmud ibn al-Rabi' who said: When the verse "Competition in worldly gain diverts you" was revealed, and he recited until he reached "Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty," they said: O Messenger of Allah, about which bounty will we be questioned? Indeed, there are only the two black things: water and dates, and our swords are on our necks, and the enemy is present. About which bounty will we be questioned? He said: "Indeed, that will come to pass."

And Ahmad said: Abu 'Amir 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Habib narrated to us, from his father, from his paternal uncle, who said: We were in a gathering when the Prophet (ﷺ) came upon us, and there was a trace of water on his head. We said: O Messenger of Allah, we see you in good spirits. He said: "Indeed." He said: Then the people began to discuss wealth (ghinā), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no harm in wealth for one who fears Allah, and health for one who fears Allah is better than wealth, and contentment of the soul (ṭīb al-nafs) is of the bounty."

Ibn Majah related it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Khalid ibn Makhlad, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman, with the same chain. [Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/158): "This chain is ṣaḥīḥ, its narrators are trustworthy."]

And al-Tirmidhi said: 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, Shababah narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Ala', from al-Dahhak ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Arzam al-Ash'ari, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah saying: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The first thing a servant will be questioned about of the bounty on the Day of Resurrection is that it will be said to him: Did We not make your body healthy, and give you cool water to drink?"

Related by al-Tirmidhi alone. Ibn Hibban related it in his Sahih by way of al-Walid ibn Muslim, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Ala' ibn Zabr, with the same wording.

And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Musaddad narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Yahya ibn Hatib, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: al-Zubayr said: When the verse "[Then] you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty" was revealed, they said: O Messenger of Allah, about which bounty will we be questioned, when there are only the two black things, dates and water? He said: "Indeed, that will come to pass." Likewise al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah related it from the hadith of Sufyan, that is Ibn 'Uyaynah, with the same wording. Ahmad related it from him. And al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan.

And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Zahrani narrated to us, Hafs ibn 'Umar al-'Adani narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from 'Ikrimah, who said: When this verse was revealed: "Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty," the Companions said: O Messenger of Allah, what bounty are we in, when we eat only barley bread in the halves of our stomachs? Then Allah revealed to His Prophet (ﷺ): Say to them: Do you not wear sandals and drink cold water? That is of the bounty.

And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn al-Asbahani informed us, from Ibn Abi Layla, I think from 'Amir, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning His saying: "[Then] you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty," he said: "Security and health." [Abd Allah ibn Ahmad related it in Zawa'id al-Zuhd (855) by way of Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Asbahani, with the same chain.]

And Zayd ibn Aslam said, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty," meaning: the fullness of stomachs, cold drink, shade of dwellings, soundness of bodies, and the pleasure of sleep. Ibn Abi Hatim related it with his earlier chain, from him, at the beginning of the surah.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Even concerning a sip of honey. Mujahid said: Concerning every pleasure of the pleasures of this world. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: The bounty of lunch and dinner. Abu Qilabah said: Among the bounties is eating honey and ghee with pure bread. The saying of Mujahid is the most comprehensive of these sayings.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning "Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty": He said: The bounty is the health of bodies, hearing and sight; Allah will question the servants about how they used them, and He knows that better than they do. This is His saying, may He be exalted: "Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart – all of those will be questioned about" (al-Isra' 17:36).

It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari, Sunan al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, by way of 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Hind, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam) said: "Two blessings many people are cheated in: health and free time."

The meaning of this is that they fall short in thanking these two blessings; they do not fulfil their due, and whoever does not fulfil the right that is incumbent upon him is cheated.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Marwazi narrated to us, 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, Abu Hamzah narrated to us, from Layth, from Abu Fazarah, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What is above the waist-wrap, the shade of a wall, and bread, for which the servant will be reckoned on the Day of Resurrection, or will be questioned about." [Musnad al-Bazzar (3643), Kashf al-Astar; Layth ibn Abi Sulaym is weak.] Then he said: We do not know it except through this chain.

And Imam Ahmad said: Bahz and 'Affan narrated to us, both said: Hammad narrated to us – 'Affan said in his narration: – Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says – 'Affan said: on the Day of Resurrection –: O son of Adam, I carried you upon horses and camels, I married you to women, and I made you enjoy and lead; so where is the thanks for that?" [Musnad Ahmad (2/492).] He alone related it by this route.

End of the tafsir of Surah "al-Takathur" [ and to Allah belongs all praise and grace ].

**Tafsir (commentary on) Surat at-Takathur**
It is a Meccan surah.
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
* *

He, may He be exalted, says: The love of this world, its pleasures and its splendour, has preoccupied you away from seeking the Hereafter and striving for it. That continued until death came to you, you visited the graves, and you became among their inhabitants?!

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Waqqar al-Misri narrated to us, Khalid ibn Abd ad-Dayim narrated to us, from Ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you﴾ from obedience, ﴿until you visit the graves﴾ until death comes to you."[[This is mu'dal (a narration with two or more consecutive narrators missing), and Abd ar-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam is weak.]]

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you﴾ refers to wealth and children.

In Sahih al-Bukhari, in its chapter "ar-Riqaq" (softening of hearts), there is: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b who said: "We used to regard this as part of the Qur'an until the revelation of ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you﴾," meaning: "If the son of Adam had a valley of gold..."

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'ba narrated to us: I heard Qatadah narrating from Mutarrif, meaning Ibn Abd Allah ibn ash-Shikhkhir, from his father, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was reciting: "﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you﴾. The son of Adam says: 'My wealth, my wealth.' But do you have from your wealth except what you eat and thereby consume, or what you wear and thereby wear out, or what you give in charity and thereby send ahead?"

Muslim, at-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i narrated it through the route of Shu'ba, with the same wording.[[Al-Musnad (4/24), Sahih Muslim no. (2958), Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (3354), and Sunan an-Nasa'i (6/238).]]

Muslim said in his Sahih: Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Hafs ibn Maysara narrated to us, from al-Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The servant says: 'My wealth, my wealth?' Of his wealth he has only three things: what he eats and thereby consumes, what he wears and thereby wears out, and what he gives in charity and thereby stores up. Everything else will go away, and he will leave it for the people." Muslim alone narrated it.[[Sahih Muslim no. (2959).]]

Al-Bukhari said: Al-Humaydi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm narrated to us, that he heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three things follow the deceased: two return and one remains with him. His family and his wealth follow him, and then his family and his wealth return, while his deeds remain."

Muslim, at-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i also narrated it through the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyayna, with the same wording.[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6514), Sahih Muslim no. (2960), Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (2379), and as-Sunan al-Kubra of an-Nasa'i no. (2064).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya narrated to us, from Shu'ba, Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The son of Adam grows old, and two things remain in him: greed and hope." Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it in their Sahihs.[[Al-Musnad (3/115), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6421), and Sahih Muslim no. (1047).]]

Al-Hafiz (the memorizer of hadith) Ibn Asakir mentioned, in the biography of al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, whose name was ad-Dahhak, that he saw a man holding a dirham, and said: "Whose is this dirham?" The man said: "Mine." He said: "It is yours only if you spend it on a reward or seeking gratitude." Then al-Ahnaf recited, quoting a line of a poet:

"You belong to wealth if you hold onto it,
but when you spend it, the wealth belongs to you."[[Tarikh Dimashq (8/443, manuscript).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Usama narrated to us, saying: Salih ibn Hayyan narrated to me, from Ibn Buraydah, concerning His words ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you﴾: it was revealed about two tribes of the Ansar, the Banu Harithah and the Banu al-Harith, who boasted to one another and competed in numbers. One of them said: "Among you is such-and-such the son of such-and-such, and such-and-such?" The others said the same. They boasted about their living members. Then they said: "Come, let us go to the graves." Each group began saying: "Among you is such-and-such?" pointing to a grave, "and such-and-such?" The others did likewise. So Allah revealed: ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you, until you visit the graves﴾, meaning: in what you have seen there is a lesson and a preoccupation.

Qatadah said: ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you, until you visit the graves﴾: They used to say, "We are more numerous than the Banu so-and-so, and we are more numerous than the Banu so-and-so," while they were falling away day by day until the end of them. By Allah, they continued like this until they all became people of the graves.

The correct view is that the meaning of His words ﴿you visit the graves﴾ is: you go to them and are buried in them. This is as is found in the Sahih: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon a Bedouin man to visit him when he was ill. He said: "Do not worry, it is a purification, if Allah wills." The man said: "A purification? Rather, it is a boiling fever upon an old man, which will bring him to the graves!" He said: "Then so be it."[[Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (5662, 5656, 7470).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'a narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Asbahani narrated to us, Hakkam ibn Salm ar-Razi informed us, from Amr ibn Abi Qays, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Minhal, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ali, who said: "We continued to doubt the punishment of the grave until the revelation of ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you, until you visit the graves﴾."

At-Tirmidhi narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Hakkam ibn Salm, with the same wording, and said: It is gharib (a hadith with a single narration path).[[Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (3355).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Salama ibn Dawud al-Ursi narrated to us, Abu al-Malih ar-Raqqi narrated to us, from Maymun ibn Mihran, who said: I was sitting with Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz when he recited ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you, until you visit the graves﴾. He paused for a while, then said: "O Maymun, I do not see the graves except as a visit, and the visitor must return to his home."

Abu Muhammad (Ibn Abi Hatim) said: That is, he must return to his home, which is either Paradise or Hellfire. It is also related that a Bedouin heard a man reciting this verse, ﴿until you visit the graves﴾, and said: "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, the people have been resurrected today!" meaning that the visitor will move from that place to another.
* *

As for His words: ﴿No! You will soon know. Then, no! You will soon know﴾, al-Hasan al-Basri said: This is a warning upon a warning.

* *

Then He said: ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire. Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾. This is an explanation of the earlier warning, His words ﴿No! You will soon know. Then, no! You will soon know﴾. He threatened them with this state, which is seeing the Fire. When it breathes out a single breath, every angel brought near and every messenger sent will fall to their knees out of awe, grandeur, and witnessing the terrors, as is related in the transmitted report concerning this.
* *

He said: "What brought you out at this hour?" He said: "What brought you out, O Messenger of Allah, brought me out." Then Umar ibn al-Khattab came, and he said: "What brought you out, O son of al-Khattab?" He said: "What brought you out brought me out." Come in, for he will come shortly, if Allah wills." She spread a rug under a tree. Abu al-Haytham came, rejoiced at them, and his eyes were delighted by them. He climbed a palm tree and cut bunches for them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "That is enough, O Abu al-Haytham." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, eat from its unripe dates, its ripe dates, and its dried dates." Then he brought them water, and they drank. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/317): "In it is Abd Allah ibn Isa, Abu Khalaf, who is weak."]] This is gharib from this route.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Husayn ibn Ali as-Sada'i narrated to me, al-Walid ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Kaysan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: While Abu Bakr and Umar were sitting, the Prophet (ﷺ) came to them and said: "What has made you sit here?" They said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, we did not leave our homes except from hunger." He said: "By the One who sent me with the truth, nothing else brought me out." So they set out until they came to the house of a man from the Ansar. The woman met them, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to her: "Where is so-and-so?" She said: "He has gone to fetch sweet water for us." Then their host came carrying his water-skin and said: "Welcome! Nothing has visited the servants that is better than what has visited me today." He hung his water-skin on the trunk of a palm tree, went off, and brought them a bunch of dates. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Why did you not pick it yourself?" He said: "I wanted you to be those whom you choose with your own eyes." Then he took the knife. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the milk-giver." So he slaughtered for them that day, and they ate. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You will surely be questioned about this on the Day of Resurrection. Hunger brought you out of your homes, and you did not return until you obtained this. This is part of the bliss."[[Tafsir at-Tabari (30/185).]]

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Yazid ibn Kaysan, with the same wording.[[Sahih Muslim no. (2038).]] Abu Ya'la and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of al-Muharibi, from Yahya ibn Ubayd Allah, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, with the same wording.[[Musnad Abi Ya'la (1/79) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3181).]] The people of the four Sunan (collections) have also narrated it, through the hadith of Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayrah, with something similar to this context and this story.[[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (5128), Sunan at-Tirmidhi nos. (2822, 2369), as-Sunan al-Kubra of an-Nasa'i no. (11697), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3745).]]

And Imam Ahmad said: Surayj narrated to us, Hashraj narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu 'Usayb, who was the freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out at night and passed by me, and he called me, so I went out to him. Then he passed by Abu Bakr and called him, and he went out to him. Then he passed by 'Umar and called him, and he went out to him. So he set off until he came to a garden (ḥā'iṭ) belonging to one of the Ansar. He said to the owner of the garden: "Feed us." So he brought a cluster of dates (dhiq) and placed it down, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions ate. Then he asked for cold water and drank, and he said: "You will certainly be questioned about this on the Day of Resurrection." He said: So 'Umar took the cluster and struck it against the ground, until the unripe dates (busr) scattered before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then he said: O Messenger of Allah, will we really be questioned about this on the Day of Resurrection? He said: "Yes, except for three things: a piece of cloth with which a man covers his private parts, or a morsel with which he stills his hunger, or a hole into which he enters to shelter from heat and cold." Related by Ahmad alone.

And Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, 'Ammar narrated to us, I heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu Bakr and 'Umar ate fresh dates (ruṭab) and drank water, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is of the bounty (naʿīm) about which you will be questioned."

Al-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah [from 'Ammar ibn Abi 'Ammar, from Jabir] with the same wording.

And Imam Ahmad said: Ahmad narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Mahmud ibn al-Rabi' who said: When the verse "Competition in worldly gain diverts you" was revealed, and he recited until he reached "Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty," they said: O Messenger of Allah, about which bounty will we be questioned? Indeed, there are only the two black things: water and dates, and our swords are on our necks, and the enemy is present. About which bounty will we be questioned? He said: "Indeed, that will come to pass."

And Ahmad said: Abu 'Amir 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Habib narrated to us, from his father, from his paternal uncle, who said: We were in a gathering when the Prophet (ﷺ) came upon us, and there was a trace of water on his head. We said: O Messenger of Allah, we see you in good spirits. He said: "Indeed." He said: Then the people began to discuss wealth (ghinā), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no harm in wealth for one who fears Allah, and health for one who fears Allah is better than wealth, and contentment of the soul (ṭīb al-nafs) is of the bounty."

Ibn Majah related it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Khalid ibn Makhlad, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman, with the same chain. [Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/158): "This chain is ṣaḥīḥ, its narrators are trustworthy."]

And al-Tirmidhi said: 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, Shababah narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Ala', from al-Dahhak ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Arzam al-Ash'ari, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah saying: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The first thing a servant will be questioned about of the bounty on the Day of Resurrection is that it will be said to him: Did We not make your body healthy, and give you cool water to drink?"

Related by al-Tirmidhi alone. Ibn Hibban related it in his Sahih by way of al-Walid ibn Muslim, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Ala' ibn Zabr, with the same wording.

And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Musaddad narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Yahya ibn Hatib, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: al-Zubayr said: When the verse "[Then] you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty" was revealed, they said: O Messenger of Allah, about which bounty will we be questioned, when there are only the two black things, dates and water? He said: "Indeed, that will come to pass." Likewise al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah related it from the hadith of Sufyan, that is Ibn 'Uyaynah, with the same wording. Ahmad related it from him. And al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan.

And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Zahrani narrated to us, Hafs ibn 'Umar al-'Adani narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from 'Ikrimah, who said: When this verse was revealed: "Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty," the Companions said: O Messenger of Allah, what bounty are we in, when we eat only barley bread in the halves of our stomachs? Then Allah revealed to His Prophet (ﷺ): Say to them: Do you not wear sandals and drink cold water? That is of the bounty.

And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn al-Asbahani informed us, from Ibn Abi Layla, I think from 'Amir, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning His saying: "[Then] you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty," he said: "Security and health." [Abd Allah ibn Ahmad related it in Zawa'id al-Zuhd (855) by way of Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Asbahani, with the same chain.]

And Zayd ibn Aslam said, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty," meaning: the fullness of stomachs, cold drink, shade of dwellings, soundness of bodies, and the pleasure of sleep. Ibn Abi Hatim related it with his earlier chain, from him, at the beginning of the surah.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Even concerning a sip of honey. Mujahid said: Concerning every pleasure of the pleasures of this world. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: The bounty of lunch and dinner. Abu Qilabah said: Among the bounties is eating honey and ghee with pure bread. The saying of Mujahid is the most comprehensive of these sayings.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning "Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty": He said: The bounty is the health of bodies, hearing and sight; Allah will question the servants about how they used them, and He knows that better than they do. This is His saying, may He be exalted: "Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart – all of those will be questioned about" (al-Isra' 17:36).

It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari, Sunan al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, by way of 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Hind, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam) said: "Two blessings many people are cheated in: health and free time."

The meaning of this is that they fall short in thanking these two blessings; they do not fulfil their due, and whoever does not fulfil the right that is incumbent upon him is cheated.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Marwazi narrated to us, 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, Abu Hamzah narrated to us, from Layth, from Abu Fazarah, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What is above the waist-wrap, the shade of a wall, and bread, for which the servant will be reckoned on the Day of Resurrection, or will be questioned about." [Musnad al-Bazzar (3643), Kashf al-Astar; Layth ibn Abi Sulaym is weak.] Then he said: We do not know it except through this chain.

And Imam Ahmad said: Bahz and 'Affan narrated to us, both said: Hammad narrated to us – 'Affan said in his narration: – Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says – 'Affan said: on the Day of Resurrection –: O son of Adam, I carried you upon horses and camels, I married you to women, and I made you enjoy and lead; so where is the thanks for that?" [Musnad Ahmad (2/492).] He alone related it by this route.

End of the tafsir of Surah "al-Takathur" [ and to Allah belongs all praise and grace ].
